docs.text: Admin ¶ Milestone M2. Everything lives under Catalog › OpenLabel : Labels (when and where) and Designs (how it looks). Designs are reusable: make one "red pill" and use it in many labels. First label in one click ¶ While there are no labels, the Labels grid shows three starters. Each creates an enabled label with a built-in design, applies it to configurable, grouped and bundle parents, and places it on the category listing and the product page: Starter Shows on Position Sale -{SAVE_PERCENT}% every discounted product top start New (30 days) products created in the last 30 days top end Only {STOCK_QTY} left products with 5 or fewer pieces left (salable quantity) bottom start The positions were checked free of collisions on the Hyvä 1.4 product card. A second click within a minute does not create a duplicate. The starter's message tells you how many products match. Labels grid ¶ Columns: status, name, design preview, where it shows ("Listing TR, Product TL"), matched products (distinct products in the index), active now (with the schedule in the shop timezone), from/to, priority and store views. Filter by name, status, store view or "active now". Click a row to edit name, status, priority or dates inline; mass actions enable, disable or delete. Every change reindexes the label and cleans the cached pages it affects. Label form ¶ Section What it does Basics Name (admin only), switch it on or off, pick a design from thumbnails (or create one in a new tab and press "Refresh designs"), priority (lower number wins), "hide other labels", "hide when a variable is zero" (e.g. leave "Only {STOCK_QTY} left" out when the quantity is 0), a link (a page of this shop such as /sale.html , or https://… ; javascript: and other schemes are refused) with "ask search engines not to follow the link", "show on configurable, grouped and bundle products". Show when Switches for the common cases — On sale (minimum discount %), New (days), Low stock (pieces left), Out of stock, Well rated (stars), Bestseller (among the top N by units sold in the last 30 days) — and the advanced rule tree for anything else (any product attribute, category, SKU, attribute set, type). A product must match the switches and the tree. Nothing switched on means every product. Show where One row per placement: page (category/search/widgets, product page, and since 1.1 the shopping cart, mini cart, wish list, compare page and order emails, where labels show as text next to the item), position with the picker (arrow keys work): the 3×3 grid on the image, the dashed band around it (above, below, left, right), or in the product text next to the price, next to Add to Cart or under the name, a different design for this page, max labels in that corner, stacking, gap, offsets and "keep left/right in RTL". Who and when Store views ("All Store Views" = everywhere), customer groups (empty = everyone), start and end in the shop timezone. A date without a time ends at the end of that day. Stored in UTC. Matched products After the first save: how many products match in the default store view, the first 50 with thumbnails, what to check when nothing matches, and Reindex now . The live preview panel (bottom right, can be hidden) renders the chosen design on a sample product with the same structural CSS as the shop: every placement of the selected page, variables filled with sample values ({SAVE_PERCENT} → 25), desktop and mobile widths, a warning when text contrast is below 4.5:1, and "Preview as" a customer group. Save, Save & Continue and Save & Duplicate (creates a disabled copy). Problems are listed above the form without a page reload, each saying what to do, for example "Pick at least one placement so the label appears somewhere." On the product page (1.1) ¶ Catalog › Products › edit a product › OpenLabel (needs the Labels permission): Labels this product shows now , from the index (any store view and customer group), each linking to its label; "(by hand)" marks the ones assigned here. Always show these labels : the product shows them whatever their conditions, within their store views, customer groups and dates. Saving the product reindexes the labels you add or remove. Assignments are not part of the export file yet; they go with their label or product when either is deleted. Designs ¶ Choose Text , Image or Shape ; the form shows only what that type needs. Text and shape: label text with a variable picker and a 24-character counter, colours with a live contrast badge (green ≥ 4.5:1, amber ≥ 3:1, red below), border, shape (rectangle, pill, circle, ribbon, corner) and rotation presets. Image: PNG, JPG, GIF, WebP, AVIF or SVG up to 1 MB (the limit is a setting; a warning above 50 KB). The real content type is checked; SVGs are cleaned (no scripts, event handlers, external references or entities). Width and height are stored so images never shift the layout. Alternative text is required. Size: percent of the product image width (default) or pixels. Optional overrides of the width and the largest font size for phones (up to 639 px wide), tablets (640–1023 px) and desktops (1024 px and up). Motion: an entry animation (fade in, pop in) that plays once, and a hover effect (grow, lift) while the shopper points at the product. CSS only; not on touch screens for hover, and never for shoppers who ask their device for reduced motion. Tooltip: optional, per store view, variables allowed (e.g. "Offer ends {SPECIAL_END_DATE}"). Shown when the shopper points at the label or moves to it with the keyboard. Text per store view: each store view uses the default text unless you untick "Use the default text". Custom CSS: only for users with the "Edit custom CSS of designs" permission; @media , @supports and @container blocks are kept; other at-rules (such as @import ), expressions, script URLs and escapes are removed before it is saved. The 31 built-in designs are locked: open one and press Duplicate to edit . Their texts follow the store view's language ( label packs ); a copy keeps the English text until you enter your own per store view. They pass WCAG AA contrast. Designs used by labels and built-in designs cannot be deleted. Settings ¶ Stores › Configuration › Iranimij › OpenLabel: Setting Default Enable OpenLabel Yes Per store view. Labels stay indexed while disabled. Default max labels per position 3 For new placements (1–10). Label indexer — Shows the current mode; "Update by Schedule" is recommended. Debug mode No Adds data-ol-label attributes to the shop markup (render package, M3). Hide labels on these pages none Page types without labels (home, category, search, product, other content pages, cart, wish list, compare); no query is made there. Flush the page cache after a change. Hide labels on these other pages empty More pages by full action name, one per line (e.g. brand_index_view ). Brand attribute (Label text variables) manufacturer The attribute {BRAND} shows. Largest image upload (Images) 1024 KB 50 to 5120 KB. Global CSS has its own section (Stores › Configuration › Iranimij › OpenLabel custom CSS) and permission: CSS added after all designs in the label stylesheet of every store, cleaned like the custom CSS of designs. Saving it rebuilds the stylesheet. Permissions ¶ ACL resource Allows Iranimij_OpenLabel::labels Labels grid, form, starters, matched products, reindex Iranimij_OpenLabel::designs Designs grid, form, uploads Iranimij_OpenLabel::custom_css Editing custom CSS of designs Iranimij_OpenLabel::global_css The global CSS settings section Iranimij_OpenLabel::config The settings section

docs.text: The engine (M1) ¶ How OpenLabel decides which label shows on which product. Everything below the admin and the storefront: schema, rule conditions, the indexer, variables, the resolver and the CLI. Written during milestone M1; the admin (M2), Hyvä rendering (M3) and GraphQL / import (M4) build on it. Data model ¶ Table Holds openlabel_label the when and where : name, status, priority (0 = highest), store views, customer groups, valid_from / valid_to (UTC), the serialized condition tree, the default design, apply_to_parent , hide_lower_priority openlabel_design the how it looks : type (text, image, shape), colours, size, rotation, custom CSS, is_system openlabel_design_store text, alt text and tooltip per store view (store 0 = default, other stores fall back to it) openlabel_placement one where per label: area ( listing , product ), position ( tl … br ), optional design override, offsets, max_labels , stacking, gap openlabel_label_product products assigned to a label by hand on the product edit page (1.1); the indexer adds them to the label's matches, still within its status, store views, customer groups and dates, and only when the product is enabled in that store openlabel_index the result: ( label_id , product_id , store_id , customer_group_id ) with the label's priority and window copied in; customer_group_id = -1 means every group Repositories: LabelRepositoryInterface saves a label with its placements, DesignRepositoryInterface saves a design with its store texts. Both validate and answer with actionable messages. A design that labels still use cannot be deleted. Everything in Api/ follows semantic versioning from 1.0. Conditions ¶ A label's conditions are a core Magento\Rule tree (ALL / ANY, nested) stored as JSON in conditions_serialized . Leaves are either the native product-attribute condition (every attribute, category, SKU, attribute set; store-scoped attributes are evaluated per store view) or one of the built-ins: Built-in Attributes Source On sale on_sale (yes/no), discount_percent (rounded half up), discount_amount price index of the store's website and the customer group, so special prices and catalog price rules both count Is new news_dates (inside Set Product as New dates, default scope), days_since_created , days_since_updated product entity Stock is_salable (yes/no), salable_qty MSI stock of the website's sales channel, legacy stock status without MSI; quantity applies to simple, virtual and downloadable products only Price range final_price , price price index Rating rating (stars) review summary of the store view Review count review_count review summary of the store view Bestseller (1.1) sold_last_7d , sold_last_30d , sold_last_90d (units), sales_rank_30d (1 = best) order items of the website's store views; canceled and refunded quantities do not count; a configurable sale counts for the configurable Most viewed (1.1) views_last_7d , views_last_30d , view_rank_30d product view events of Magento's reports ( report_event ; keep product view reports enabled) Ships free (1.1) free_shipping (yes/no) an active cart rule without coupon and without conditions that gives free shipping to the website and group, or the product's final price (price index) reaching the free shipping method's minimum order amount Operators. Numeric built-ins offer is , is not , equals or greater than , greater than , equals or less than , less than , is one of and is not one of (e.g. "days since created is less than 30", "salable quantity is one of 1, 2, 3"). Yes/no built-ins offer is and is not . Native attributes keep Magento's operators for their type (text: contains, is one of…; dates: is, on or after, on or before; category: is, is not, is one of…). Every condition is tested with every operator it offers ( Test/Integration/Model/Condition/OperatorMatrixTest ). Missing data never matches , whatever the operator, is not included: a product without a price index row for price conditions, without a rating for rating , without a stock row (and composites) for salable_qty , and a product without a value for a product attribute condition (e.g. "news from date on or before 2020-01-01" does not pick up products without that date). A product without reviews has review_count 0, so "review count is 0" finds products nobody reviewed yet. Likewise products without sales or views count 0 units / 0 views but have no rank , so "bestseller rank at most 10" only picks products that sold. This holds on every supported Magento version: 2.4.7 and 2.4.8 would otherwise treat missing values as 0. Daily refresh. Bestseller, most viewed, ships free and the "days since" conditions change with time, not with product saves: labels using them are reindexed by the daily cron ( openlabel_daily_is_new , despite its name it covers every time-dependent condition), so a new bestseller appears within a day. Run bin/magento openlabel:reindex <label_id> to refresh one sooner. Matching happens in SQL: the tree is attached to a product collection with Iranimij\OpenLabel\Model\Rule\SqlBuilder , the core rule builder with three changes. It keeps the joins of every condition when it recurses into nested groups (the core one drops those collected before a nested group, which broke quick switches combined with advanced conditions). And it writes the SQL of every condition itself (the core operators, without the IFNULL(field, 0) of 2.4.7 and 2.4.8), so the rules above hold on every Magento version. And a condition may join a bounded subquery instead of a table (the 7/30/90-day sales and view counts with their RANK() ). PHP validate() exists on every condition for previews and tests. Custom conditions: extend Iranimij\OpenLabel\Model\Condition\AbstractBuiltIn and register the class in the Iranimij\OpenLabel\Model\Condition\ConditionPool types argument. Two consequences worth knowing: Price-based conditions read the price index. Depending on the Magento version and Display Out of Stock Products , the price index may omit out-of-stock products; those then get no price labels. Errors while matching are logged to var/log/openlabel.log (with the label and its conditions); the admin shows the cause and keeps the label saved. Disabled products never match. Children of configurable, grouped and bundle products do, which is what apply_to_parent builds on. Indexer ¶ openlabel_product (Index Management › OpenLabel Products ) depends on the price and stock indexers. Full reindex builds into openlabel_index_replica , computes the products that gained or lost a label, swaps the tables atomically and cleans the full page cache for exactly those products. A lock prevents two full reindexes from overlapping. Partial reindex (Update on Save, or the changelog in Update by Schedule) rebuilds the rows of the changed products plus their configurable / grouped / bundle parents and siblings. Per label : saving a label rebuilds its rows at once, whatever the indexer mode, and cleans the cache for the diff plus the openlabel_<id> tag. Deleting a label drops its rows. openlabel:reindex <id> and the daily cron do the same. Rows : one per store view the label is limited to (all active store views otherwise). One row per allowed customer group when the label is limited to groups or uses a price condition, otherwise one row with customer_group_id = -1 . With apply_to_parent , a parent gets a row when any child matches; the row remembers the lowest matching child in parent_product_id . Triggers : mview subscriptions on the product, category, website, relation, stock item and review summary tables; plugins on the price indexer ( Rows , Full ), the stock indexer and review aggregation so price, stock and review changes arrive even though index tables are never subscribed (that would flood the changelog). A full price or stock reindex invalidates the OpenLabel index. Time : valid_from / valid_to are copied into the index and filtered at resolve time, so no cron activates labels. Two small crons remain: hourly, clean the cache of labels whose window opened or closed during the last hour (a label can therefore appear up to one hour late on cached pages); daily, rebuild labels whose conditions depend on the date ("is new", days since created). Known 1.0 limitation : on multi-source MSI shops, source-item changes that bypass the legacy stock item reach the index on the next product save, stock indexer run or full reindex. Variables ¶ Label text may contain variables, substituted at render time from the already loaded product (no extra queries for prices and stock): {SAVE_PERCENT} {SAVE_AMOUNT} {PRICE} {SPECIAL_PRICE} {FINAL_PRICE} {STOCK_QTY} {NEW_FOR} {SKU} {ATTR:code} {BR} {SPECIAL_ENDS_IN} {SPECIAL_END_DATE} {RATING} {REVIEW_COUNT} {SOLD_LAST_30D} {CATEGORY_NAME} {BRAND} {COUNTDOWN} Numbers, currency amounts and dates are formatted for the store's locale. Values are escaped; the text itself may use b strong i em br span small sup sub (attributes other than class , id , title , style are removed). Unknown variables stay literal so typos are visible. A zero number renders as "0" and is reported as empty: a label with Hide when a variable is zero on is left out on such products (storefront and GraphQL). The label is dropped after the priority rules, so it does not free its place in a full stack, and its "hide other labels" still applies. {RATING} , {REVIEW_COUNT} , {SOLD_LAST_30D} and {CATEGORY_NAME} load their data once per listing through VariablePreloadInterface ; {SPECIAL_ENDS_IN} treats special_to_date as valid through that day. {COUNTDOWN} is the time left until the special price ends ("2d 04:12:09", the end of its last day like {SPECIAL_ENDS_IN} ), ticked every second by the theme script; screen readers read the end date instead. Markup produced by variables ( {BR} , {COUNTDOWN} ) keeps its attributes; the allow-list cleans the merchant's text only. {CATEGORY_NAME} is the category being browsed on a category page. Everywhere else (product page, search, widgets, GraphQL) it is the product's deepest active category in the store's tree, never the category the shopper came from, so cached pages stay correct. Renaming a category updates labels on that category's pages at once and elsewhere when the product's page cache is next cleaned. {BRAND} shows the attribute set under Stores › Configuration › Iranimij › OpenLabel › Label text variables (default manufacturer ), like {ATTR:code} ; on listings the attribute needs "Used in Product Listing". Custom variables implement Iranimij\OpenLabel\Api\VariableProcessorInterface and are registered in the Iranimij\OpenLabel\Model\Variable\Pool processors argument. Resolver ¶ Iranimij\OpenLabel\Api\LabelResolverInterface::getForProducts(int[] $productIds, int $storeId, int $customerGroupId) runs one SELECT over the index joined with labels, placements, designs and store texts, filtered by status, UTC time window and customer_group_id IN (-1, group) , then arranges the rows: priority order, hide_lower_priority (a matching label with the flag suppresses labels with a higher priority number on that product), and the per-stack limit (a stack is one area + position; its limit is the max_labels of its highest-priority label). Templates use Iranimij\OpenLabel\ViewModel\Labels : call getForProducts() once with every product id of the page, then getStacks($productId, 'listing') per item. Results are memoized per request; the customer group comes from the HTTP context, which the full page cache already varies on. When openlabel/general/enabled is off for the store, the view model returns nothing without a query. Budget, enforced by integration tests with a query counter: a listing of 36 products costs one query, a product page costs one query. CLI ¶ bin/magento openlabel:reindex # full rebuild through the indexer (lock, swap, cache diff) bin/magento openlabel:reindex 3 # one label, prints the diff bin/magento openlabel:preview 3 --store=1 # matched count and the first 20 SKUs from the index

docs.text: Table Holds openlabel_label the when and where : name, status, priority (0 = highest), store views, customer groups, valid_from / valid_to (UTC), the serialized condition tree, the default design, apply_to_parent , hide_lower_priority openlabel_design the how it looks : type (text, image, shape), colours, size, rotation, custom CSS, is_system openlabel_design_store text, alt text and tooltip per store view (store 0 = default, other stores fall back to it) openlabel_placement one where per label: area ( listing , product ), position ( tl … br ), optional design override, offsets, max_labels , stacking, gap openlabel_label_product products assigned to a label by hand on the product edit page (1.1); the indexer adds them to the label's matches, still within its status, store views, customer groups and dates, and only when the product is enabled in that store openlabel_index the result: ( label_id , product_id , store_id , customer_group_id ) with the label's priority and window copied in; customer_group_id = -1 means every group Repositories: LabelRepositoryInterface saves a label with its placements, DesignRepositoryInterface saves a design with its store texts. Both validate and answer with actionable messages. A design that labels still use cannot be deleted. Everything in Api/ follows semantic versioning from 1.0.

docs.text: A label's conditions are a core Magento\Rule tree (ALL / ANY, nested) stored as JSON in conditions_serialized . Leaves are either the native product-attribute condition (every attribute, category, SKU, attribute set; store-scoped attributes are evaluated per store view) or one of the built-ins: Built-in Attributes Source On sale on_sale (yes/no), discount_percent (rounded half up), discount_amount price index of the store's website and the customer group, so special prices and catalog price rules both count Is new news_dates (inside Set Product as New dates, default scope), days_since_created , days_since_updated product entity Stock is_salable (yes/no), salable_qty MSI stock of the website's sales channel, legacy stock status without MSI; quantity applies to simple, virtual and downloadable products only Price range final_price , price price index Rating rating (stars) review summary of the store view Review count review_count review summary of the store view Bestseller (1.1) sold_last_7d , sold_last_30d , sold_last_90d (units), sales_rank_30d (1 = best) order items of the website's store views; canceled and refunded quantities do not count; a configurable sale counts for the configurable Most viewed (1.1) views_last_7d , views_last_30d , view_rank_30d product view events of Magento's reports ( report_event ; keep product view reports enabled) Ships free (1.1) free_shipping (yes/no) an active cart rule without coupon and without conditions that gives free shipping to the website and group, or the product's final price (price index) reaching the free shipping method's minimum order amount Operators. Numeric built-ins offer is , is not , equals or greater than , greater than , equals or less than , less than , is one of and is not one of (e.g. "days since created is less than 30", "salable quantity is one of 1, 2, 3"). Yes/no built-ins offer is and is not . Native attributes keep Magento's operators for their type (text: contains, is one of…; dates: is, on or after, on or before; category: is, is not, is one of…). Every condition is tested with every operator it offers ( Test/Integration/Model/Condition/OperatorMatrixTest ). Missing data never matches , whatever the operator, is not included: a product without a price index row for price conditions, without a rating for rating , without a stock row (and composites) for salable_qty , and a product without a value for a product attribute condition (e.g. "news from date on or before 2020-01-01" does not pick up products without that date). A product without reviews has review_count 0, so "review count is 0" finds products nobody reviewed yet. Likewise products without sales or views count 0 units / 0 views but have no rank , so "bestseller rank at most 10" only picks products that sold. This holds on every supported Magento version: 2.4.7 and 2.4.8 would otherwise treat missing values as 0. Daily refresh. Bestseller, most viewed, ships free and the "days since" conditions change with time, not with product saves: labels using them are reindexed by the daily cron ( openlabel_daily_is_new , despite its name it covers every time-dependent condition), so a new bestseller appears within a day. Run bin/magento openlabel:reindex <label_id> to refresh one sooner. Matching happens in SQL: the tree is attached to a product collection with Iranimij\OpenLabel\Model\Rule\SqlBuilder , the core rule builder with three changes. It keeps the joins of every condition when it recurses into nested groups (the core one drops those collected before a nested group, which broke quick switches combined with advanced conditions). And it writes the SQL of every condition itself (the core operators, without the IFNULL(field, 0) of 2.4.7 and 2.4.8), so the rules above hold on every Magento version. And a condition may join a bounded subquery instead of a table (the 7/30/90-day sales and view counts with their RANK() ). PHP validate() exists on every condition for previews and tests. Custom conditions: extend Iranimij\OpenLabel\Model\Condition\AbstractBuiltIn and register the class in the Iranimij\OpenLabel\Model\Condition\ConditionPool types argument. Two consequences worth knowing: Price-based conditions read the price index. Depending on the Magento version and Display Out of Stock Products , the price index may omit out-of-stock products; those then get no price labels. Errors while matching are logged to var/log/openlabel.log (with the label and its conditions); the admin shows the cause and keeps the label saved. Disabled products never match. Children of configurable, grouped and bundle products do, which is what apply_to_parent builds on.

docs.text: openlabel_product (Index Management › OpenLabel Products ) depends on the price and stock indexers. Full reindex builds into openlabel_index_replica , computes the products that gained or lost a label, swaps the tables atomically and cleans the full page cache for exactly those products. A lock prevents two full reindexes from overlapping. Partial reindex (Update on Save, or the changelog in Update by Schedule) rebuilds the rows of the changed products plus their configurable / grouped / bundle parents and siblings. Per label : saving a label rebuilds its rows at once, whatever the indexer mode, and cleans the cache for the diff plus the openlabel_<id> tag. Deleting a label drops its rows. openlabel:reindex <id> and the daily cron do the same. Rows : one per store view the label is limited to (all active store views otherwise). One row per allowed customer group when the label is limited to groups or uses a price condition, otherwise one row with customer_group_id = -1 . With apply_to_parent , a parent gets a row when any child matches; the row remembers the lowest matching child in parent_product_id . Triggers : mview subscriptions on the product, category, website, relation, stock item and review summary tables; plugins on the price indexer ( Rows , Full ), the stock indexer and review aggregation so price, stock and review changes arrive even though index tables are never subscribed (that would flood the changelog). A full price or stock reindex invalidates the OpenLabel index. Time : valid_from / valid_to are copied into the index and filtered at resolve time, so no cron activates labels. Two small crons remain: hourly, clean the cache of labels whose window opened or closed during the last hour (a label can therefore appear up to one hour late on cached pages); daily, rebuild labels whose conditions depend on the date ("is new", days since created). Known 1.0 limitation : on multi-source MSI shops, source-item changes that bypass the legacy stock item reach the index on the next product save, stock indexer run or full reindex.

docs.text: Label text may contain variables, substituted at render time from the already loaded product (no extra queries for prices and stock): {SAVE_PERCENT} {SAVE_AMOUNT} {PRICE} {SPECIAL_PRICE} {FINAL_PRICE} {STOCK_QTY} {NEW_FOR} {SKU} {ATTR:code} {BR} {SPECIAL_ENDS_IN} {SPECIAL_END_DATE} {RATING} {REVIEW_COUNT} {SOLD_LAST_30D} {CATEGORY_NAME} {BRAND} {COUNTDOWN} Numbers, currency amounts and dates are formatted for the store's locale. Values are escaped; the text itself may use b strong i em br span small sup sub (attributes other than class , id , title , style are removed). Unknown variables stay literal so typos are visible. A zero number renders as "0" and is reported as empty: a label with Hide when a variable is zero on is left out on such products (storefront and GraphQL). The label is dropped after the priority rules, so it does not free its place in a full stack, and its "hide other labels" still applies. {RATING} , {REVIEW_COUNT} , {SOLD_LAST_30D} and {CATEGORY_NAME} load their data once per listing through VariablePreloadInterface ; {SPECIAL_ENDS_IN} treats special_to_date as valid through that day. {COUNTDOWN} is the time left until the special price ends ("2d 04:12:09", the end of its last day like {SPECIAL_ENDS_IN} ), ticked every second by the theme script; screen readers read the end date instead. Markup produced by variables ( {BR} , {COUNTDOWN} ) keeps its attributes; the allow-list cleans the merchant's text only. {CATEGORY_NAME} is the category being browsed on a category page. Everywhere else (product page, search, widgets, GraphQL) it is the product's deepest active category in the store's tree, never the category the shopper came from, so cached pages stay correct. Renaming a category updates labels on that category's pages at once and elsewhere when the product's page cache is next cleaned. {BRAND} shows the attribute set under Stores › Configuration › Iranimij › OpenLabel › Label text variables (default manufacturer ), like {ATTR:code} ; on listings the attribute needs "Used in Product Listing". Custom variables implement Iranimij\OpenLabel\Api\VariableProcessorInterface and are registered in the Iranimij\OpenLabel\Model\Variable\Pool processors argument.

docs.text: Iranimij\OpenLabel\Api\LabelResolverInterface::getForProducts(int[] $productIds, int $storeId, int $customerGroupId) runs one SELECT over the index joined with labels, placements, designs and store texts, filtered by status, UTC time window and customer_group_id IN (-1, group) , then arranges the rows: priority order, hide_lower_priority (a matching label with the flag suppresses labels with a higher priority number on that product), and the per-stack limit (a stack is one area + position; its limit is the max_labels of its highest-priority label). Templates use Iranimij\OpenLabel\ViewModel\Labels : call getForProducts() once with every product id of the page, then getStacks($productId, 'listing') per item. Results are memoized per request; the customer group comes from the HTTP context, which the full page cache already varies on. When openlabel/general/enabled is off for the store, the view model returns nothing without a query. Budget, enforced by integration tests with a query counter: a listing of 36 products costs one query, a product page costs one query.

docs.text: GraphQL ¶ OpenLabel adds one field to ProductInterface , so every product type in every product query has it: { products(filter: { sku: { eq: "24-MB04" } }) { items { sku openlabel_labels { id name type text image_url alt position area css_class bg_color text_color priority } } } } Field Meaning id , name Label ID and admin name type Design type: text , image or shape text Text for the store view with variables filled in, as plain text ( {BR} becomes a line break). null for image labels image_url , alt Image labels only position on the image tl tc tr ml mc mr bl bc br ; around it above_l above_c above_r below_l below_c below_r left_t left_m left_b right_t right_m right_b ; in the product text near_price near_cart under_name area listing , product , cart , minicart , wishlist , compare or email css_class The ol-* classes the storefront uses; load the generated stylesheet to reuse them bg_color , text_color Hex colours of the design priority 0 is the highest tooltip Tooltip for the store view with variables filled in, plain text; null without one (1.1) click_url , click_nofollow Click-through link ( https:// , http:// or a shop path starting with / ) and whether it should carry rel="nofollow" (1.1) Rules ¶ One entry per placement: a label shown on listings and on the product page appears twice, once per area . The store view comes from the Store header, the customer group from the customer token (guests are NOT LOGGED IN). Only enabled labels inside their time window and allowed for that group are returned; conditions are never exposed. Configurable, grouped and bundle products return the labels of matching children when the label has "apply to parents" on, like the storefront. All products of one query cost one label query (batch resolver), however many products the query returns. With the module disabled for a store view the field returns an empty list. Asking for openlabel_labels makes the product query load the price attributes the variables need, so {SAVE_PERCENT} , {PRICE} and friends match the storefront. {ATTR:code} shows a value only when the query also asks for that attribute (the storefront has the same rule: the attribute must be loaded on the page). Caching ¶ GET queries are cacheable. Responses carry the tags openlabel_<label_id> and openlabel_design_<design_id> , which label and design saves clean, plus the usual product tags. Customers' queries vary by customer group through Magento's X-Magento-Cache-Id : send the value of the previous response back, as Magento's own clients do, and Varnish serves logged-in customers from the cache too.

docs.text: Do not put container-type: inline-size on Hyvä's image anchor. a.product-item-photo is block mx-auto inside a flex flex-col card, so it is shrink-to-fit: its width comes from the image. Inline-size containment removes that size source and the anchor collapses to 0 × 0 (verified; the Playwright spec keeps a test for this). The same applies to any wrapper OpenLabel inserts inside the anchor. The listing container is therefore the product card ( .product-item , w-full in the grid): .product-item { container-type: inline-size } causes no layout shift (verified on desktop and mobile), and label sizes in cqw relate to the card width, which on Hyvä equals the image column. The .ol-anchor wrapper stays position: relative; display: block without containment. On the product page #gallery-main is a block with a definite width ( w-full parent), so #gallery-main { container-type: inline-size } is safe (verified). Absolutely positioned elements on the card (FE5): only the swatch radio inputs ( input.absolute.product-option-value-input , visually under the swatch buttons, below the image) and sr-only helpers. Nothing overlaps the image area, so all four corners are free for labels.

docs.text: Listing, next to the price: Plugin\PriceBoxPlugin appends the stack to Magento\Catalog\Pricing\Render\FinalPriceBox in the item_list zone (every product card, widget and slider). Listing, under the name and next to Add to Cart: the card has no child block there, so Plugin\ListItemPlugin inserts the stacks right after a.product-item-link and [data-addto="cart"] of the rendered Magento_Catalog::product/list/item.phtml . Cards without those elements keep their markup. Product page: Plugin\InlineSlotPlugin appends the stacks after the layout elements product.info.title , product.info.price and product.info.addtocart . A theme that renames them adds its names to the productPageSlots argument of the plugin in etc/frontend/di.xml . All three render inside the cached card or page, tagged like the image labels; no JavaScript.

docs.text: Block\ProductLabels renders LabelRenderer::getProductPageStacksHtml() : for a configurable product the stacks also hold each variant's labels (the product's own labels plus the variant's, arranged by priority), hidden with ol-label--hidden and tagged data-ol-variant . Parent and variants are resolved with one query. Block\Script ( openlabel.script in before.body.end , template js/labels.phtml ) is rendered only when the page needs it ( LabelRenderer::isScriptNeeded() , also set by product cards served from the block cache). It listens to configurable-selection-changed and ticks .ol-countdown[data-ol-end] ; the inline script is registered with $hyvaCsp->registerInlineScript() .

docs.text: Hyvä 1.5 rebuilt the product gallery as a snap slider: #gallery (a <section> , a grid column of the product page) → div.relative (positioned wrapper with the navigation buttons and the gallery.additional container) → #gallery-main[data-track] , the horizontally scrolling track with one slide per image. Slot: Plugin\GalleryPlugin recognises the track by data-track and inserts the label stacks right before it, inside the positioned wrapper. Labels stay on the visible image while the shopper swipes; inside the track they would scroll away with the first slide. Container-query root: #gallery (only when it holds labels, :has ). Containment must not go on the track or the wrapper: the wrapper is a shrink-to-fit flex item on desktop, and inline-size containment collapses the whole gallery to zero width (found by the 1.5 end-to-end leg). On 1.3/1.4 the root stays #gallery-main . Previous/next buttons: they sit in a bottom corner of the image ( bottom-2 end-2 , or the start corner with the theme's "start" setting) above the track. Labels placed in that corner move up 3.25 rem, above the buttons, or they would be covered and not clickable (found by the 1.1 end-to-end leg). The rule is keyed on the buttons being in the markup, so nothing moves after Alpine starts. Listings are unchanged in 1.5: the image link of the product card is the slot, the card is the root. docs.text: Export and import ¶ Keep labels in git, copy them from staging to production, or share a set of labels with another shop. bin/magento openlabel:export var/openlabel.json # every label bin/magento openlabel:export var/sale.json --labels=3,7 # some labels bin/magento openlabel:export > labels.json # to stdout bin/magento openlabel:import var/openlabel.json --dry-run # check only bin/magento openlabel:import var/openlabel.json # add the labels bin/magento openlabel:import var/openlabel.json --replace # update labels and designs with the same name What the file contains ¶ One JSON document: {"format": "openlabel", "version": 2, "designs": [...], "labels": [...]} . Labels: name, status, priority, schedule (UTC), condition tree, apply to parents, hide lower priority, hide when a variable is zero, click-through link and its nofollow flag, and the placements with their per-area design. Designs: every design the exported labels use, with all store-view texts, the custom CSS, the entry animation, the hover effect and the per-breakpoint sizes. Image designs carry the image file (base64), so the file is self-contained. Versions: OpenLabel 1.1 writes version 2 and still reads version 1 files from OpenLabel 1.0; the fields added in 1.1 then take their defaults (no animation, no link, no size overrides). Built-in designs are referenced by name ( system:<name> ) and are never copied: the importing shop uses its own. Store views and customer groups are referenced by code ( default , General , Wholesale ), not by id, so a file works in a shop whose ids differ. The admin store view is admin . How an import behaves ¶ All or nothing. The whole file is checked against the shop first, and nothing is written when anything is wrong; the command lists what to fix: Nothing was imported. Fix these and run again: - labels[0] "Sale": this shop has no store view with code "de". Checked before anything is written: store view and customer group codes, design references, condition classes (only OpenLabel's and those registered in its condition pool), the same rules as the admin forms, images (type, size, SVG sanitizing, as for uploads) and custom CSS (sanitized as in the design form). Then designs, images and labels are written in one database transaction, and each label is indexed as it is saved. Without --replace , labels and designs are always added, so importing the same file twice gives two copies. With --replace , a label or design with the same name is updated instead; built-in designs are never changed. An image that already exists with the same content is reused; a different file with the same name gets a new name, so existing designs never change their picture. Moving from the Smile product label module ¶ bin/magento openlabel:import-smile --dry-run bin/magento openlabel:import-smile The command reads the smile_productlabel tables directly, so it works even after the Smile module was disabled (keep its tables and pub/media/smile_productlabel/imagelabel/ until you are done). Every Smile label becomes: an image design Smile: <name> with the label's image and alt text (18 % of the image width; adjust it in the design form), a label with the same name, status and store views, the condition " is ", and a placement on listings and/or the product page at the same corner ( top-left → top left, lower-right → bottom right, …). Labels whose name already exists in OpenLabel are skipped, so you can run the command again after fixing a problem. A Smile label whose image file or attribute is missing is reported and skipped; everything else goes through the same checks and the same single transaction as openlabel:import . Importers for paid modules are not part of 1.0.

docs.text: Install and upgrade ¶ Requirements ¶ Magento Open Source, Mage-OS or Adobe Commerce 2.4.7, 2.4.8 or 2.4.9, PHP 8.2 to 8.4. For the storefront on Hyvä: the Hyvä default theme 1.4 or 1.5 (1.3: best effort). Other themes: see Custom themes . MSI is optional. Remote storage (Magento_RemoteStorage, e.g. Amazon S3): OpenLabel writes its stylesheets and label images through Magento's filesystem, so it should work, but it is not tested yet. Install ¶ composer require iranimij/openlabel-hyva-bundle bin/magento setup:upgrade bin/magento openlabel:reindex The bundle installs iranimij/openlabel (core), iranimij/openlabel-hyva (Hyvä storefront) and iranimij/module-base (the "Iranimij" configuration tab). Without Hyvä, require iranimij/openlabel only. In production mode also run, as for any module: bin/magento setup:di:compile bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy bin/magento cache:flush No theme build is needed: the storefront CSS is generated by OpenLabel into pub/media/openlabel/<store_id>/openlabel.<hash>.css on first use and after every label or design change. After installing ¶ Catalog › OpenLabel › Labels: create a first label from a starter ( Admin ). Stores › Configuration › Iranimij › OpenLabel: enable or disable per store view, default max labels per position, debug mode, "Regenerate CSS". Indexer: openlabel_product runs after the price and stock indexers. "Update by schedule" is recommended as for every indexer; the hourly and daily OpenLabel cron jobs need Magento's cron. Upgrade ¶ composer update iranimij/openlabel-hyva-bundle --with-dependencies bin/magento setup:upgrade bin/magento openlabel:reindex # production mode: new admin scripts and templates bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy setup:upgrade rebuilds the label stylesheet of every store, so the new version's styles reach the shop at once. Upgrade notes for each version are in the CHANGELOG . Everything in Api/ follows semantic versioning: no breaking change within 1.x. Uninstall ¶ bin/magento module:uninstall -r Iranimij_OpenLabelHyva Iranimij_OpenLabel Removes the modules, the openlabel_* tables and OpenLabel's configuration. With a plain Composer remove, run bin/magento setup:upgrade afterwards; the tables stay until you drop them.

docs.text: REST API ¶ From 1.1, labels and designs can be created, read, changed and deleted over Magento's REST API, for example by a PIM or ERP that adds a "Clearance" label during its product import. The storefront needs none of this: product labels for headless storefronts come from GraphQL . Access ¶ Every call needs a token of an admin user or an integration. The role decides what the token may do: Routes Permission (System › Permissions › User Roles › Role Resources) /V1/openlabel/labels… Catalog › OpenLabel › Labels ( Iranimij_OpenLabel::labels ) /V1/openlabel/designs… Catalog › OpenLabel › Designs ( Iranimij_OpenLabel::designs ) custom CSS of a design also Edit custom CSS of designs ( Iranimij_OpenLabel::custom_css ) TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST https://shop.example/rest/V1/integration/admin/token \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"username":"api-user","password":"…"}' | tr -d '"') curl -s https://shop.example/rest/V1/openlabel/labels/12 -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" Without a token, or with a role that lacks the permission, the answer is 401 . Routes ¶ Method and path What it does GET /V1/openlabel/labels/:labelId One label with its placements GET /V1/openlabel/labels?searchCriteria… Labels matching Magento search criteria (filters, sort, pages) POST /V1/openlabel/labels Creates a label: body {"label": {…}} PUT /V1/openlabel/labels/:labelId Replaces the label: body {"label": {…}} DELETE /V1/openlabel/labels/:labelId Deletes the label GET /V1/openlabel/designs/:designId One design GET /V1/openlabel/designs?searchCriteria… Designs matching search criteria POST /V1/openlabel/designs Creates a design: body {"design": {…}} PUT /V1/openlabel/designs/:designId Replaces the design: body {"design": {…}} DELETE /V1/openlabel/designs/:designId Deletes the design (refused while labels use it) PUT replaces the whole entity: send every field, as GET returned it, with your changes. Fields left out take their defaults. created_at and updated_at may be sent back; they are ignored. A saved label is matched to its products at once, and the pages that show it are cleaned from the cache, exactly as when it is saved in the admin. A saved design rebuilds the label stylesheet. A label ¶ { "label": { "name": "Clearance", "status": 1, "priority": 5, "design_id": 2, "store_ids": [], "customer_group_ids": [], "valid_from": null, "valid_to": "2026-12-31 23:59:59", "conditions_serialized": "{\"type\":\"Iranimij\\\\OpenLabel\\\\Model\\\\Rule\\\\Condition\\\\Combine\",\"aggregator\":\"all\",\"value\":\"1\",\"conditions\":[{\"type\":\"Iranimij\\\\OpenLabel\\\\Model\\\\Rule\\\\Condition\\\\Product\",\"attribute\":\"sku\",\"operator\":\"()\",\"value\":\"24-MB01, 24-MB04\"}]}", "apply_to_parent": true, "hide_lower_priority": false, "hide_on_zero_variable": false, "click_url": "/sale.html", "click_nofollow": false, "placements": [ { "area": "listing", "position": "tr" }, { "area": "product", "position": "tl", "max_labels": 2 } ] } } status : 1 enabled, 0 disabled. priority : 0 is the highest. store_ids , customer_group_ids : empty means all. valid_from , valid_to : UTC, or null . conditions_serialized : the conditions as JSON text in Magento's rule format, the same as in an export file . The easiest way to get it right is to build the conditions in the admin once and read the label with GET . Empty or null matches every product. Placements: area is listing , product , cart , minicart , wishlist , compare or email ; position as in GraphQL . The other placement fields ( offset_x , offset_y , max_labels , stacking , gap , pin_physical_side , sort_order ) are optional. Products assigned by hand on the product edit page are not part of the label in the API. A design ¶ { "design": { "name": "Clearance (orange)", "type": "shape", "shape": "pill", "bg_color": "#c2410c", "text_color": "#ffffff", "size_mode": "percent", "width": 24, "font_size": 14, "animation": "none", "hover_effect": "grow", "sizes": { "sm": { "width": 40 } }, "store_texts": { "0": { "text": "Clearance -{SAVE_PERCENT}%", "tooltip": "Only while stock lasts" }, "2": { "text": "Abverkauf -{SAVE_PERCENT}%" } } } } store_texts maps a store view ID to its text , alt_text and tooltip ; 0 is the default for all store views. In answers it is a JSON object, or a list when the IDs are 0, 1, 2…, where the position is the store ID. Both forms can be sent back. sizes holds overrides for phones ( sm ), tablets ( md ) and desktops ( lg ): width and font_size . Image designs ( "type": "image" ): upload the image in the admin first, then use its image_path (e.g. designs/clearance.png ). Paths of files that were not uploaded there are refused. custom_css is saved only when the token's role has "Edit custom CSS of designs"; otherwise the design keeps the CSS it had. It is sanitized like in the admin. The built-in designs ( "system": true ) cannot be changed or deleted, and a new design cannot be marked as built in. Errors ¶ Status When 400 The entity breaks a rule, e.g. no placement, an unknown position, a link starting with javascript: . The answer lists every problem under errors . Also for built-in designs and images that were not uploaded. 401 No token, or the role lacks the permission 404 No label or design with that ID

docs.text:
Storefront ¶ How labels reach the shop (milestone M3). Theme specifics for Hyvä are in hyva-integration.md . What the shopper's browser gets ¶ HTML first. Labels are rendered on the server inside the cached page, with no inline styles. Tooltips, links, animations and hover effects are CSS only. JavaScript is added only where a page needs it: the live countdown and labels that follow the chosen variant. The script is small and registered with Hyvä's CSP helper, so a strict Content Security Policy needs no exception. One stylesheet per store view , pub/media/openlabel//openlabel..css (about 8 KB, 2 KB compressed, for the 31 built-in designs; ≤ 20 KB for 100 designs). It holds the structural ol-* rules, one custom-property line per design and per placement with offsets, and the sanitized custom CSS. The file name changes with its content, so the web server can cache it for a year (Magento's sample nginx and Apache configs already do for pub/media ). No theme build needed. Nothing depends on Tailwind: labels are positioned and styled by that stylesheet, also on a theme that was never rebuilt after installing OpenLabel. bin/magento hyva:config:generate still lists the module for theme builds that want to scan it. The stylesheet is rebuilt after every design or label save, by Stores › Configuration › Iranimij › OpenLabel › Regenerate CSS , and by: bin/magento openlabel:css:regenerate Run it after copying a database or pub/media between environments. On a fresh install the file is written on the first storefront request. Previous files stay two days so pages still in Varnish keep their stylesheet. If your media URL is on another host (a CDN), allow that host in your style-src CSP policy. Markup contract (stable from 1.0) ¶ Sale -25% Class Meaning ol-stack , ol-stack--v / --h positioned container of one corner, vertical or horizontal stacking ol-pos-ts te tc ms mc me bs bc be position with logical sides (start/end): mirrors in right-to-left stores ol-pos-tl tr ml mr bl br placements set to "keep left/right in RTL" ol-pos-ots otc ote obs obc obe ost osm osb oet oem oeb the bands just outside the image (1.1): o(utside) + t(op), b(ottom), s(tart side), e(nd side) + the place along it; over the space around the image ol-pos-otl otr obl obr olt olm olb ort orm orb the bands with "keep left/right in RTL" ol-label--link the label is an (click-through, 1.1); never inside the product card's image link, where labels stay ol-has-tip + ol-tip a label with a tooltip: the next sibling is shown on hover and focus and referenced by aria-describedby ; outside links the label is focusable ( tabindex="0" ) ol-label--hidden , data-ol-variant="" product page of a configurable product (1.1): every variant's labels are in the page; 0 is the product as it opens, the others stay hidden until that variant is chosen ol-countdown ( data-ol-end , an aria-hidden ticking part, an ol-sr end date) the {COUNTDOWN} variable (1.1) ol-inline--cart / --minicart / --wishlist / --compare the row of labels of an item list (1.1): after the item name on the cart, wish list and compare pages, next to the item price in the mini cart ol-inline , ol-inline--near-price / --near-cart / --under-name labels in the product text (1.1): part of the text flow, always side by side, sized by the design's font size ol-p- offsets and gap of that placement (custom properties) ol-label , ol-label--text / --image / --shape , ol-d- , ol-shape-* the badge data-ol-label="" only with Debug mode on Custom properties: --ol-bg --ol-fg --ol-border --ol-bw --ol-w --ol-rot --ol-op --ol-fs-min --ol-fs-cq --ol-fs-max --ol-gap --ol-ox --ol-oy --ol-z . All rules use a single class, without !important , so a theme overrides them with two classes, for example .product-item .ol-stack { --ol-z: 20; } . JavaScript: none for display. Only pages with a {COUNTDOWN} or variant labels get one small inline script (openlabel-hyva, under 1 KB gzipped, registered for the CSP): one timer for all countdowns, paused in background tabs, and the switch between variant labels on Hyvä's configurable-selection-changed event (the labels of a variant show when exactly one variant matches the choice). Labels have pointer-events: none : clicks, hover image swaps and swatches work through them. Labels with a tooltip or a link (1.1) take the pointer; inside a product card a click on them still opens the product. Text sizes use container queries on the product card and the gallery, with an 11 px floor on small cards and phones. Order emails (1.1) ¶ Labels of the "Order emails" area appear under the item name in order, invoice, shipment and credit memo emails (

after

of the core item templates). Email clients ignore stylesheets, so each label is a with inline styles built from the design's colours and shape; image designs are left out (many clients block images). docs.text: HTML first. Labels are rendered on the server inside the cached page, with no inline styles. Tooltips, links, animations and hover effects are CSS only. JavaScript is added only where a page needs it: the live countdown and labels that follow the chosen variant. The script is small and registered with Hyvä's CSP helper, so a strict Content Security Policy needs no exception. One stylesheet per store view , pub/media/openlabel/<store_id>/openlabel.<hash>.css (about 8 KB, 2 KB compressed, for the 31 built-in designs; ≤ 20 KB for 100 designs). It holds the structural ol-* rules, one custom-property line per design and per placement with offsets, and the sanitized custom CSS. The file name changes with its content, so the web server can cache it for a year (Magento's sample nginx and Apache configs already do for pub/media ). No theme build needed. Nothing depends on Tailwind: labels are positioned and styled by that stylesheet, also on a theme that was never rebuilt after installing OpenLabel. bin/magento hyva:config:generate still lists the module for theme builds that want to scan it. The stylesheet is rebuilt after every design or label save, by Stores › Configuration › Iranimij › OpenLabel › Regenerate CSS , and by: bin/magento openlabel:css:regenerate Run it after copying a database or pub/media between environments. On a fresh install the file is written on the first storefront request. Previous files stay two days so pages still in Varnish keep their stylesheet. If your media URL is on another host (a CDN), allow that host in your style-src CSP policy.
